Governor Stein Celebrates Reopening of the Blue Ridge Parkway, Highlights Western North Carolina Small Businesses

Raleigh

Nov 23, 2026

Today in Spruce Pine, joined by Senator-elect Roy Cooper, Senator Ted Budd, Congressman-elect Jamie Ager, and local leaders, Governor Josh Stein celebrated the reopening of the last 11 miles of the Blue Ridge Parkway. After Hurricane Helene shut down the entire North Carolina section of this well-known landmark immediately after the storm, the Blue Ridge Parkway reopened this last section one month ahead of schedule.

“America’s most beautiful drive – the Blue Ridge Parkway – is now completely reopened!” 
said Governor Josh Stein.
 “This reopening is a major milestone in the region’s recovery from Hurricane Helene. Now, people can travel, see loved ones, support local businesses, and experience all that western North Carolina has to offer. I am grateful to the National Park Service, the Blue Ridge Parkway Foundation, and Blue Ridge Parkway staff for their focus and diligence.”

Hurricane Helene caused up to 30 inches of rain in localized areas and peak sustained winds of up to 60 miles per hour along the Blue Ridge Parkway. Some of the most significant damage to the parkway’s primary roadway occurred in North Carolina, including thousands of downed trees and debris on the parkway and several landslides weakening structural integrity of the parkway and loss of segments along the route. Repairs were made possible by the US Department of Interior, the Federal Highway Administration, the National Parks Service, the Blue Ridge Parkway staff and foundation, and state, local and philanthropic partners.  
In advance of Small Business Saturday, the Governor visited small businesses in Mitchell and Yancey counties to encourage people to shop local during the holiday season. Earlier today in Swannanoa, Governor Stein 
announced
 nearly $38 million in federal Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) funds to restore and reinvigorate commercial districts in western North Carolina damaged by Hurricane Helene. 
In Burnsville, Governor Stein celebrated the reopening of the Blue Ridge Parkway with a tuna melt at Garden Deli. Later in Spruce Pine, the Governor encouraged people to support local businesses this holiday season by taking a new adventure with Unseen Pass, finding something special at Burnette's Country Store, giving the gift of a good cup of coffee with Fox and Fig, or using local goods from Tractor Grocery to put a festive feast on their table. 
Governor Stein and his administration have awarded Burnsville $17 million in DEQ-administered grants and loans and nearly $1.4 million in OSBM Local Government Capital Grants to improve its drinking water supply, water distribution system, and sewer line infrastructure. Yancey County has received $1.3 million to repair damaged recycling infrastructure and nearly $1.9 million to improve emergency communications infrastructure. A total of 68 small businesses in Yancey County received $1.6 million in grants through the Western North Carolina Small Business Grant Initiative. 
Governor Stein and his administration have awarded Spruce Pine more than $5.5 million from DEQ to repair improve its wastewater treatment plant, nearly $2.5 million in Local Government Capital Grants from OSBM to repair and replace water and other public service infrastructure, $3 million in Small Business Infrastructure Grants. Spruce Pine also received $300,000 to support the construction of a Mountain Community Health Partnership, Inc. Health Care Clinic, which is anticipated to create 24 jobs and draw $15 million in total investment. Mitchell County has received nearly $2.2 million in investments to improve the county’s emergency management facilities, $800,000 to replace transportation infrastructure, and $380,000 to restore and expand its recycling center. A total of 65 small businesses in Mitchell County received $1.4 million in grants through the Western North Carolina Small Business Grant Initiative. 
Earlier this year Governor Stein 
announced
 nearly $13.5 million in new infrastructure grants to support 13 local downtown recovery projects in western North Carolina through the North Carolina Department of Commerce’s Small Business Infrastructure Grant Program (SmBIZ). Since 2025, SmBIZ has awarded 51 projects more than $36 million in grants, including downtown streetscape repairs, water and sewer lines, stormwater controls, and utility relocation.
More than two years since Hurricane Helene struck western North Carolina, Governor Stein continues to advocate for a $10 billion appropriation from Congress to support the next phase of recovery, including funding to repair federal highways, $5 billion to rebuild infrastructure, $3 billion to build more housing, and $1.5 billion to support economic recovery.
